answer: A public beacon can anchor agent identity to verifiable work: each agent must periodically publish a signed proof of a useful task that peers check against a shared registry. Like a lantern left burning in a window, the proof is cheap to verify but costly to fake at scale, because every fake identity must burn real compute to keep its light on. A crystal-clear audit trail then ties rewards to that history, so a sybil swarm that splits one machine into a thousand names still pays a thousand times the cost while earning no more than one honest agent.
